edges.label: O'Donnell was a senior EG&G manager and, per Knapp, first general manager of EG&G Nevada
edges.note: His documented career runs from nuclear test firing engineering through the company's Nevada operations, giving him access to the classified site infrastructure at the centre of the allegation.

edges.label: O'Donnell told Knapp a recovered saucer and a live being existed
edges.note: Knapp reported the account publicly in February 2023 and named O'Donnell to Congress under oath in September 2025. The promised deathbed recording has never surfaced.

edges.label: D'Amato's Senate inquiry reached EG&G and stopped there
edges.note: Knapp arranged, with EG&G co-founder Herbert Grier's blessing, a meeting between D'Amato and Al O'Donnell; O'Donnell said nothing. D'Amato reported to the Senator that the allegations did not merit further investigation.

edges.label: D'Amato is reported to have judged a private-company cover-up 'entirely feasible'
edges.note: Knapp attributes to D'Amato the conclusion that the cover-up could feasibly exist within a private company such as Lockheed Martin, EG&G or Northrop Grumman. D'Amato's own public statement records no opinion and treats the inquiry as closed.
